newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Heinz-Watties cuts jobs in Gisborne plant.
newsitem.headline: Heinz-Watties cuts jobs in Gisborne plant.

text.p: Food processor Heinz Wattie on Tuesday announced it would shift its petfood and prepared food operations to Hawke's Bay, with a loss of 172 jobs in Gisborne.
It will keep its Gisborne frozen sweetcorn facility, but is looking for a local business partner to own and run the corn processing plant.
Staff were told of the restructuring at a meeting in the city this afternoon.
The move will create about 100 jobs in Hastings and it was hoped some people from the Gisborne plant would transfer to Hawke's Bay.
Company chief executive David Irving said the reorganisation of its Gisborne businesses was needed to make it more cost-effective and competitive in the market place.
Reviews of the businesses had confirmed that manufacturing performance could be improved by consolidating the two Gisborne operations with the company's major facilities in Hastings.
"Unfortunately there are serious manufacturing limitations imposed by the petfood site which result in inherent inefficiencies," Irving said.

The Gisborne plant was virtually at the end of its working life which meant reinvestment had to be considered. The remoteness of the two businesses in comparison to Hastings was also a competitive handicap, he said.
Given these factors it was decided a better decision for growth would be achieved by consolidation with its other major operation in Hawke's Bay.
Heinz Wattie will spent NZ$18 million revamping its Hastings facility to accommodate the operations.
Irving said the relocation would improve the company's operating costs.
"In petfood this move will accelerate our success in the domestic market against imported Australian product and grow our export business particularly in Japan and Taiwan," he said.
The relocation would also mark Watties as a far more serious player in the frozen prepared meal category which had grown 40 percent in the past year.
Most of the jobs to be lost are in its petfood operation.
Heinz Wattie Frozen Foods employs about 20 full-time staff and the decision was not expected to impact on those jobs. During the corn season more than 100 seasonal workers were employed.

Irving said a new operator would pack for Heinz Wattie under contract, in a strategic partnership deal. Watties would maintain its involvement in growing and processing and there were no plans to shed suppliers.
A new owner would assure there would be employment at the processing plant employment. Crops other than sweetcorn and peas might be considered and organic crops were in increasing demand.
